title: Predicting surgical outcomes for chronic exertional compartment syndrome using a machine learning framework with embedded trust by interrogation strategies
summary: Retrospective military CECS cohort analysis reports a specific 12-month return-to-work prediction result: linear SVM AUC 0.85 ± 0.08, with explicit sample and generalizability limits. Repeated nested fivefold CV (30 repeats), held-out test folds. Single-facility retrospective military cohort; external prospective validation remains required.
ai_technology: Methods use clinician-informed feature selection and linear SVM to predict work return after CECS fasciotomy.

evidence.tested: 132 procedures/119 patients; six outliers removed; 126 records; best SVM AUC 0.85 ± 0.08, accuracy 0.80 ± 0.07.
evidence.unknown: Repeated nested fivefold CV (30 repeats), held-out test folds. Single-facility retrospective military cohort; external prospective validation remains required. The source does not establish benefits beyond the reported evaluation.
evidence.ai_role: Methods use clinician-informed feature selection and linear SVM to predict work return after CECS fasciotomy.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
